notes:
Quick CRM notes and call snippets:
- Product: in-app onboarding copilot that runs guided flows inside web app; must keep step response <300ms median and <700ms p99 for good UX.
- Workload profile: mostly short-turn dialog (4-12 tokens user prompts, 20-200 tokens responses) + occasional longer step summaries (~600 tokens). High concurrency during onboarding waves (100-300 concurrent sessions).
- Cost sensitivity: token caps per session (soft cap 1,200 tokens, hard cap 2,500) and strict monthly spend alerts. Team said: "We need predictable unit economics—can't have wild monthly spikes."
- Technical asks: streaming + tool-calling support (open URL, lookup customer data, call internal webhook), deterministic latency under variable seq len, prefix caching for repeated flow steps.
- Model preferences: prefer open/quantized variants for cost; interested in Redwood-recommended quantization profile and batch tuning. Willing to start on hosted API; if throughput grows want Dedicated pools (VPC) with dedicated GPU and SLA.
- Security: SSO (SAML), SOC2 required for vendor, KMS/HSM for encryption keys, audit logs exported to their SIEM, 3-year retention for event logs in certain regulated customers.
- POC success criteria: 1) streaming p50 <250ms, p95 <500ms for typical steps; 2) cost per active session <= $0.03 on average after batching/cache tuning; 3) safe tool-calling sandboxing verified; 4) security review signoff.
- Quote: requested comparison hosted vs dedicated delta for predictable throughput at 300-500 sessions/min and burst to 1000 sessions/min.
- Objection: procurement worried about vendor lock; SE suggested multi-model routing + exportable model metadata as mitigations.
- Action items assigned: Maya to deliver detailed pricing scenarios by 2026-03-12; Liam to prepare POC runbook + traffic replay script; GrovePath to share sample traffic (anonymized) and security contact.
- Direct quote from Head of Product: "Streaming reliability is table stakes — if onboarding feels laggy we lose conversion. Also want caps so a single marketing surge doesn't blow our bill."
